analysis.title: What to watch in the week ahead
key_insights: UBS expects the US midterms on 3 November to change the balance of power in Congress. Narrow majorities and presidential authority should limit sweeping policy changes, so UBS does not treat the result as a binary directional event for equities, bonds, or the dollar.

UBS midterm probabilities: 50% Democratic sweep of Congress, 40% split control (Democrats win the House, Republicans keep the Senate), 10% Republicans retain both chambers. That is a 90% chance of divided government or a Democratic sweep, and the base case is that Democrats control at least one chamber.

Democratic control could soften or delay some spending cuts. Debt-ceiling negotiations in 2027 may create volatility and result in less fiscal tightening than currently expected. The president keeps considerable authority over tariffs, foreign policy, and regulation.
UBS does not expect a change in congressional control to derail data center expansion, since many relevant decisions are made at state and local levels.
UBS still expects Treasury yields to settle slightly lower over the next 12 months, as easing inflation should prove more powerful than persistent fiscal concerns.

US tech stocks fell last week on questions about AI buildout returns despite strong earnings. The Nasdaq Composite fell 2.9% on Friday and 2.0% over the week. The S&P 500 fell 1.8% on Friday and 0.6% over the week.

AI demand data stayed strong: Google Cloud revenue +103% y/y, Microsoft Azure +48%, Oracle growth accelerated to 62%, Microsoft reported an eightfold increase in large Copilot accounts, and Alphabet said Gemini reached 1 billion users.

Investors are weighting overinvestment, financing, monetization, and cannibalization risks more heavily. Alphabet kept its USD 195-205bn 2026 capex plan, reported negative quarterly free cash flow, and indicated a further increase in 2027. Meta raised the low end of its 2026 spending range to USD 135-145bn.

Neoclouds (GPU-rental infrastructure providers) are about 8% of UBS's capex estimate versus roughly 80% for Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft, Meta, and SpaceX. UBS sees select delays, repricing, and consolidation as more likely than a collapse in spending.

UBS raised its aggregate AI capex forecasts to USD 1.0tr in 2026 and USD 1.4tr in 2027, and introduced USD 1.5tr for 2028. It stays constructive on AI and favors financially strong platforms and quality infrastructure providers over concentrated single-stock positions.

The Fed and ECB held rates last week. The Fed upgraded its growth assessment to 'strong' and two policymakers favored a 25bp hike. Chair Kevin Warsh was more dovish, citing improving inflation expectations and tighter financial and credit conditions.
Futures price close to three Fed hikes over the next 12 months. UBS calls this too hawkish and expects 25bp hikes in December and March.

The week's data includes PMIs, Eurozone inflation, US job openings, and the October US employment report. The Bank of England meets Thursday, and UBS expects a 25bp hike on accelerating UK services and core inflation.

UBS recommends diversified equity exposure and selective additions to short and medium-duration high-quality bonds, with caution on the longest maturities and lower-quality credit. Fixed income stays rated Attractive. The 10-year US Treasury yield fell to a seven-week low of 4.93% last week.

sector_views.rationale: Rated Attractive. Quality bonds offer income and diversification. Prefer short and medium duration high-quality bonds, stay cautious on the longest maturities and lower-quality credit.
Constructive on AI with strong demand, but the performance bar is rising. Favors diversified exposure to high-quality beneficiaries over single-stock concentration.

earnings_insights: Alphabet kept its 2026 capex plan at USD 195-205bn, reported negative quarterly free cash flow, and indicated higher capex in 2027 (reported last week).
Google Cloud revenue grew 103% y/y, Microsoft Azure 48%, and Oracle's growth accelerated to 62% (reported last week).
Meta raised the low end of its 2026 capex range to USD 135-145bn (reported last week).
Apple reports this week, among other quarterly earnings reports UBS flags for investors to watch.

risk_factors: Debt-ceiling negotiations in 2027 and tougher fiscal negotiations under a changed Congress.
AI overinvestment, financing (especially neoclouds), monetization, and cannibalization risks.
Stronger price pressures or renewed growth and employment momentum could push rate expectations higher.
Higher energy and input costs spreading into broader prices.
Eurozone inflation becoming more evident in underlying inflation rather than staying energy-driven.
vol_and_positioning: UBS says volatility could go up in the near term around the midterms, including through debt-ceiling negotiations in 2027, but expects macroeconomics and stock fundamentals to matter more for markets.
geopolitical: US midterm elections on 3 November will determine control of Congress, with focus on government borrowing, trade policy, and regulation.
Debt-ceiling negotiations in 2027 may create volatility.
The president retains considerable authority over tariffs, foreign policy, and regulation.

tension_points.bull_case: AI demand remains strong: Google Cloud +103% y/y, Azure +48%, Oracle 62%, and an eightfold increase in large Copilot accounts. Neoclouds are only about 8% of UBS's capex estimate versus roughly 80% for the five largest spenders.
tension_points.bear_case: Investors weigh overinvestment, financing, monetization, and cannibalization risks. Alphabet reported negative quarterly free cash flow and signaled higher 2027 capex, and slower monetization in existing businesses shows adoption does not translate quickly into profit growth.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Select delays, repricing, and consolidation among neoclouds would mark the bear case spreading, though UBS says a collapse in spending is less likely.

tension_points.bull_case: Warsh struck a dovish tone, citing improving inflation expectations and tighter financial and credit conditions. UBS expects only 25bp hikes in December and March.
tension_points.bear_case: The Fed upgraded growth to 'strong', two policymakers favored a hike, and futures price close to three hikes in 12 months.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Stronger price pressures or renewed momentum in growth and employment in the PMIs, Eurozone inflation, job openings, and October payrolls data could push rate expectations higher.
